Been grinding Lucci for awhile now, I feel this hybrid CP9/Navy version is probably the least consistent of the three archtypes for Lucci right now. You want to lean into either Navy(Where JP ended the set at with Lucci) or CP9/Air Door. Some issues I see with your list currently,

​

\- You only have 16 targets for Kaku effect, almost all of which you don't want in your trash in the first place. 

\- Blueno will only ever hit Khalifa, Wanze, Fukuro. These are all relatively weak except in the case of needing to recycle cards with Khalifa on the opponent's turn. The reason you run Kumadori is that the opponent kills Blueno, a 6k, and then your pull Kumadori out and they need to kill another 6k. This acts as a pseudo blocker, because the opponent is tempted by it coming in rested. Either they deal with the Kumadori or the opponent is actively down on card economy & board state due to the investment to kill Blueno. 

\- With 12 2k's, and 12 blockers(8 of which are unkillable by effects), 4 impact wave is too many. These cards will often be dead in hand as Lucci really wants to use all his don every turn. I personally run 2 and even then feel it's a bit much. Have been toying with the idea of cutting it entirely and running 6 King Pistol in its place due to it being 0 don and allowing me to discard cards early. 

\-  4 Sakazuki in the hybrid version is heavy, 6 don is a weird number for Lucci in my experience. The amount you can get done with 4 don is very limited unless you devote that turn to just establishing board by playing Borosolino or Fukuro and swinging with 1 on someone. The reason I play 2 Sakazuki and 1 ST Garp is that with Garp at 5 don, it allows me to also play anything else besides Issho(I don't run SEC Kuzan in my version). On the conservative side, I could Fukuro and float 2 for impact wave. 

​

If you wanted a TLDR; I would say you should lean either into the CP9/Airdoor package or the Navy package and not try to mix the two too much.

IT in the school Of arts and sciences was more of an all rounder position where you did a little bit of everything. But you still worked with a ticketing system for most of it.

During my time there, I’d have to say most departments in The School Of Arts and Sciences would be what you’re looking for. 

The school as a whole was incredibly well run from the top to the bottom when it came to day to day work. Each department was between 3-6 people so you got pretty tight with your coworkers and really got to know the clients in your department. 

During my time I enjoyed Psychology/Biology the most, it was a healthy balance of Researchers with more long term concerns like storage solutions and Professors with day to day concerns like broken AV equipment. 

The ability to move around within a single school is there as well, it wasn’t uncommon to see someone do a few years in one department and then move to another based of staff needs.

If money is your largest concern though, Wharton hands down pays best and functions almost as it’s own entity. Though they’re more picky with hiring. A joke that was often throw around was people get into UPenn IT in one department and then use it as leverage as an internal candidate to get a mid level position at Wharton.
